id: 第四章-终点篇-河童-十五-p1

en: 第四章-终点篇-河童-十五
About a week later, I happened to hear Doctor Chaka tell of a strange incident.
u.src: 大概过了一个星期，我偶然听医生查喀说起一件奇闻。

en: Rumor had it that Tock's house was haunted.
u.src: 传闻说托喀家闹鬼。

en: By then, the female kappa who had lived there had gone off somewhere, and Tock's house had become a photography studio.
u.src: 那会儿，原来那只雌河童不知道去哪了，托喀的家变成了摄影工作室。

en: According to Chaka, whenever customers came to this studio to have their photographs taken, Tock's shadow would always appear faintly behind them.
u.src: 听查喀说，每当有顾客来这间工作室拍照，后面总是隐约出现托喀的影子。

en: There was no doubt that Chaka was a materialist, and he did not believe in ghosts after death.
u.src: 毫无疑问，查喀是个唯物主义者，不相信死后有幽灵。

en: When he spoke about it, he smiled maliciously and said, "In that case, the soul must also have a material existence."
u.src: 他说这件事的时候，也不怀好意的笑着，说：“这么说来灵魂这个东西也是有物质的存在哩。”

en: I thought the same way as Chaka, and neither of us believed in ghosts.
u.src: 我跟查喀想法一样，都不相信有幽灵。

en: But I felt warmly toward the poet Tock, so I went to a bookstore and bought a stack of newspapers and magazines carrying photographs of Tock's ghost and related reports.
u.src: 但是我对诗人托喀怀有好感，于是到书店买了一批刊有托喀的幽灵的照片和刊有相关新闻的报刊。

en: Sure enough, in these photographs, behind male and female kappa of all sizes, one could faintly make out a kappa that looked like Tock.
u.src: 果不其然，在这些照片上，在大大小小的雌雄河童身后，能够模模糊糊辨认出一只像是托喀的河童。

en: What surprised me most was not Tock's ghost appearing in the photographs, but the related report provided by the Society for Psychic Studies.
u.src: 照片上出现的托喀的幽灵倒不是最让我吃惊的，而是灵学会提供的相关报告。

en: I translated the report in detail and have written a summary of its contents below.
u.src: 我把报告详细的翻译出来了，把内容梗概写在下面。

en: The notes in parentheses are comments I added myself.
u.src: 括号里的是我自己加的注释。

en: Report concerning the ghost of the poet Tock, published in issue 8274 of the Journal of the Society for Psychical Studies.
u.src: 《有关诗人托喀君的幽灵的报告》（刊载于灵学会杂志第八二七四期。）

en: Not long ago, we members of the Spiritualist Society gathered at the former home of Tock, the poet who had killed himself,
u.src: 不久之前，我们灵学会会员在自杀的诗人托喀君的故居、

en: now the studio of a certain photographer, at No. 251 on XX Street, and held a temporary investigation meeting.
u.src: 现为某某摄影师的工作室的××街第二五一号举办了临时调查会。

en: The members present were as follows.
u.src: 出席的会员如下。
（姓名从略）

en: At ten thirty in the morning on September seventeenth, the seventeen of us members gathered in that studio with Mr. Peka, president of the Society for Spiritual Studies, and with Mrs. Hepp, the medium we trusted most.
u.src: 九月十七日上午十点三十分，我等十七名会员与灵学会会长培喀先生，偕同我等最信任的灵媒赫卟夫人，齐聚该工作室。

en: As soon as Mrs. Hepp entered the room, she sensed a ghostly presence, and at once her whole body went into spasms and she could not stop vomiting.
u.src: 赫卟夫人刚一走进屋里，马上感触到鬼气，随即全身痉挛，呕吐不已。

en: According to the lady, this was because the poet Toka had been fond of smoking while alive, so even his ghostly aura contained nicotine, or so she said.
u.src: 根据夫人所称，这是因为诗人托喀君生前嗜好吸烟，他的鬼气里也含有尼古丁云云。

en: We members sat quietly around the round table with Mrs. Hepp.
u.src: 我等会员与赫卟夫人静静地坐在圆桌四周。

en: After three minutes and twenty-five seconds, the lady suddenly fell into a very violent state of somnambulism,
u.src: 三分二十五秒以后，夫人突然陷入非常激烈的梦游状态，

en: and she was possessed by the soul of Toka, the poet.
u.src: 并且被诗人托喀君的灵魂附体。

en: We members, in order of age,
u.src: 我等会员以年龄为顺序，

en: held the following dialogue with the spirit of Toka, who had possessed the lady:
u.src: 和附体在夫人身上的托喀君的魂灵对话如下：

en: Question: Why do you appear as a spirit?
u.src: 问：你为什么显灵呢？

en: Answer: mainly to know what my reputation would be after my death.
u.src: 答：主要是为了知道我死后的名声。

en: Question: Do you -- or rather, do all of you present here -- ghosts, still care about your reputation in the world of the living?
u.src: 问：你——或是说在座的各位，幽灵仍旧在意俗世的名声吗？

ja: にせずにはいられない。
en: Answer: at least I cannot help caring about it.
u.src: 答：至少我做不到不在意。

en: But the ghost of a Japanese poet I once met cared nothing at all for fame after death.
u.src: 但是我所遇到的一位日本诗人的幽灵却在死后对名声毫不在意。

en: Question: Do you know who this poet is?
u.src: 问：你知道这位诗人是谁吗？
答：很遗憾忘记了。

en: I only remember one of the seventeen-syllable poems he liked to compose.
u.src: 我只记得他喜欢作的十七字诗中的一首。

en: Question: What is that poem about?
u.src: 问：那首诗里讲的是什么？

en: Answer: That ancient pond, ah; a frog jumped into the water and made a clear, ringing sound.
u.src: 答：那古老的池塘啊，青蛙跳到水里，发出了清脆的声响。

en: Question: do you think this poem is well written?
u.src: 问：你觉得这首诗写得好吗？

en: Answer: I think it is very well written.
u.src: 答：我觉得写的很好。

en: However, it would be even more wonderful if "frog" could be changed to "kappa."
u.src: 不过，要是能把“青蛙”换成“河童”就更美妙了。

en: Question: What was the reason for that?
u.src: 问：因为什么原因呢？

ja: いだそうとしているからです。
en: Answer: Because we kappa are eager to find the image of kappa in every form of art.
u.src: 答：因为我们河童在所有的艺术里面，都急切地想要找到河童的形象。

en: At that moment, Chairman Pekka reminded the seventeen of us members that this was a special investigation meeting of the Society for Psychical Research, not a meeting for criticism.
u.src: 这个时候，会长培喀先生提醒我等十七名会员，这是灵学会的临时调查会，并不是评论会。

en: Question: How is life for you spirits?
u.src: 问：各位魂灵的生活怎么样？

en: Answer: There is not much difference between me and all of you.
u.src: 答：与诸位没甚差别。

en: Question: So do you regret choosing suicide?
u.src: 问：那么你后悔选择自杀吗？

en: Answer: I do not regret it.
u.src: 答：并不后悔。

en: If I grow tired of life as a ghost, I can also use a pistol to be "resurrected."
u.src: 倘若幽灵生活过烦了，我也可以用手枪“复活”。
问：“复活”，容易做到吗？

en: Mr. Toka's ghost answered the question with another question.
u.src: 托喀君的幽灵用另一个反问回复了这个问题。

en: For the kappa who knew Mr. Toka well, this kind of answer was not surprising.
u.src: 对于熟悉托喀君的河童来说，这种回答不足为奇。

en: Answer: Is suicide easy to carry out?
u.src: 答：自杀，容易做到吗？
问：各位的生命是永恒的吗？

en: Answer: There are many different theories about our life.
u.src: 答：关于我们的生命，有各种各样的说法。

en: Never forget that, fortunately, among us there are also many different religions, such as Christianity, Buddhism, Islam, and Zoroastrianism.
u.src: 千万不要忘记，幸亏我们当中也有基督教、佛教、伊斯兰教、拜火教等各种宗教。

en: Question: What religion do you believe in?
u.src: 问：你信仰什么宗教？

en: Answer: I have always been a skeptic.
u.src: 答：我一直是个怀疑派。

en: Question: But you do not doubt the existence of ghosts, do you?
u.src: 问：但是你应该不怀疑幽灵的存在吧？

en: Answer: I am not as unquestioningly convinced as all of you are.
u.src: 答：我没有诸位那么深信不疑。

en: Question: How many friends do you have?
u.src: 问：你有多少个朋友？

en: Answer: The friends I have made, from every age and every country, number no fewer than three hundred in all.
u.src: 答：我交的朋友，古今中外加起来不下三百个。

ja: クライスト、マインレンダー、ワイニンガーなどである……
en: Among the famous ones are Kleist, Mainländer, Weininger...
u.src: 其中著名的有克莱斯特、迈兰德、魏宁格尔……

en: Question: Did all the friends you associated with kill themselves?
u.src: 问：你所结交的朋友都是自杀的吗？
答：也不全是。

en: Montaigne, who defended suicide, is also one of the friends I respect.
u.src: 为自杀作辩护的蒙坦也是我的尊敬的朋友之一。

ja: ショーペンハウアーの
en: But I do not associate with pessimists who lack the courage to kill themselves, people like Schopenhauer and his kind.
u.src: 可是我不和不敢自杀的厌世主义者来往，诸如叔本华之流的人。

ja: ショーペンハウアーは
u.src: 问：叔本华还健在吗？

en: Answer: At present, he has founded ghostly pessimism and is discussing whether he can bring himself back to life.
u.src: 答：他目前创立了幽灵厌世主义，正在讨论能否自我“复活”。

en: But ever since he learned that cholera, too, is a disease caused by bacteria, he seems to have felt much more at ease.
u.src: 但是自从他知道了霍乱也是细菌引起的疾病之后，似乎安心了很多。

ja: ドストエフスキー、ダーウィン、
en: We members then asked him about Napoleon, Confucius, Dostoevsky, Darwin,
u.src: 我等会员接着跟他打听拿破仑、孔子、陀思妥耶夫斯基、达尔文、

en: Cleopatra, Shakyamuni, Demosthenes, Dante, Sen no Rikyu, and the news of other ghosts like them.
u.src: 克莉奥佩特拉、释迦牟尼、德漠斯特涅斯 、但丁、千利休等幽灵的消息。

en: Unfortunately, Mr. Tock was unable to answer in detail.
u.src: 遗憾的是托喀君没能详细地回答。

en: Instead, Mr. Tock asked us in return about the various rumors and gossip concerning him.
u.src: 托喀君却反问起那些和他有关的种种流言蜚语。

en: Question: What was my reputation like after I died?
u.src: 问：我死后了之后名声怎么样？

en: Answer: A critic described you as "one of the minor poets."
u.src: 答：一位评论家评论你是“小诗人之一”。

en: Question: He is probably one of the kappa who bears a grudge because I did not give him a copy of my poetry collection.
u.src: 问：他恐怕是因为我没有赠送它诗集而怀恨在心的河童之一吧。

en: Has my complete collection of poetry been published?
u.src: 我的诗歌全集出版了吗？

en: Answer: It was published, but it did not sell well.
u.src: 答：出版了，但是卖的不好。

en: Question: Three hundred years from now—once they have entered the public domain—tens of thousands of people will be rushing to buy my complete works.
u.src: 问：三百年后——等到公版之后，我的全集将为数万人争先抢购。

ja: どうなったのだろうか？
en: What will have become of the girlfriend who was living with me?
u.src: 跟我同居的女友怎么样了呢？

en: Answer: She is now the wife of Mr. Raka, the bookseller.
u.src: 答：她现在是书商拉喀君的夫人了。

en: Question: Unfortunately, she still does not know that Mr. Laka's eyes are fake.
u.src: 问：遗憾的是她还不知道拉喀君的眼睛是假的。
那么我的儿子呢？

en: Answer: I hear he is currently in the national orphanage.
u.src: 答：听说目前是在国立孤儿院里。

en: Tock was silent for a while, then began asking questions again.
u.src: 托喀君静默了一会儿，又问起来了。
问：我的家呢？

en: Answer: It is now a photographer's studio.
u.src: 答：现在是某摄影师的工作室。
问：我的书桌呢？

en: Answer: No one knows where it is.
u.src: 答：没人知道它的下落。

ja: にしまっているのですが——
en: Question: I have kept a bundle of letters treasured in the drawer of that desk—
u.src: 问：我在那张书桌的抽屉里珍藏着一束信件——

en: But that has nothing to do with all of you busy people.
u.src: 不过这跟忙碌的诸位没什么关系。

en: Our ghostly realm will soon enter twilight.
u.src: 我们幽灵界马上就进入黄昏了。

en: I must take my final leave of you all.
u.src: 我要和各位诀别。
再见，各位。
再见，善良的各位。

en: As soon as the final words had been spoken, Mrs. Hepp suddenly came back to her senses.
u.src: 最后一句话刚说完，赫卟夫人猛然清醒过来了。

en: We seventeen members swear before God that this conversation is true and trustworthy.
u.src: 我等十七名会员向在神起誓，这番对话是真实可信的。

en: Besides, Mrs. Hepp, who trusted us, has already been paid according to the daily wage she used to receive when she was an actress.
u.src: （再说了，对我等信任的赫卟夫人的报酬，已经按照夫人过去当女演员时的日薪标准付过去了。）
